body:
qa#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibw6yXcLi9aRRBpPT4W

**Slice api** of the qa#3 R2-TOUCH increment (70 of the 147 items of the wave selector; the browser slice, 53 items, and the P2 slice, 24 items, file their own records). The full per-clause tables follow as seven comments, one per runner group.


## Environment fingerprint

- framework objectstack-ai/objectstack **main @ ee9ad834** (`fix(objectql, runtime): a function's bare-name record follows its holders …` #32877); `ui/` in the same tree, **no Console build** (every item in this slice is api / cli / build surface).
- Wave: qa#3 seat #33014, anchor #32908, round-2 early increment (R2-TOUCH), maintainer 2026-11-13 04:10Z 「先跑，有问题可以同步解决」.
- Build: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (24 s) + `turbo build` of the showcase, CLI and dogfood closures (70 packages, 5 m 15 s, 0 cached). Node 22.23.4, pnpm 10.31.0, 4 CPUs.
- App: stock showcase (`examples/app-showcase`) via `objectstack dev --seed-admin -p PORT -d file:/tmp/qa3/db/ITEM.db --no-compile --no-watch` with `OS_PORT=PORT`; one port + one file DB per item in seven disjoint ranges 4610–4679. Scratch app copies under /tmp/qa3/scratch for CLI items, scratch packages and any boot that needed its own compiled stack. Walled `isolated` / `group` boots were started by hand from the tree with the posture env vars (qa-fixture `walled-boot` compiles into the shared dist, so it was not used).
- Seed: `--seed-admin` (admin@objectos.ai) + the showcase's demo personas; runtime personas, keys and permission sets minted per item through HTTP doors (named in each clause row).
- Execution: **parallel**, 7 runner subagents at effort `high` (4 Tier 1 by area, 3 Tier 2), dispatched from this thread session. Timestamps 04:11Z (start) → 04:52Z (last runner done).
- Wall-clock: setup 7 min (install, build, selector, smoke boot) · testing 33 min wall on 7 parallel runners (each runner self-reported 6–10 min of its own setup: reading, helpers, boots). Cost at draft time: `get_session` `external_metadata.usage.cost_usd` = 74.15.

## Scope

Selector `touched:5fb79bc0` resolved at ee9ad834 by `node scripts/checklist-select.mjs touched:5fb79bc0 --json` → 147 runnable items (4 blocked hidden; 333 files changed in 5fb79bc0..HEAD). This slice = `items-api.md`: 70 items (48 Tier 1 pinned, 22 Tier 2 manual). Every item's `revision` below is the one the resolver reported (all 70 matched the item JSON read by the runners). No `planned` item is in this slice.

Method: Tier 1 ran every pin file named in each item's `automated.ref` (one vitest invocation per package per runner; ui/e2e playwright specs not run: browser surface). **All pins green at ee9ad834** (L1 unit 593 tests / dogfood 83; L2 637 unit + 16 dogfood; L3 2,965 unit/integration + 164 dogfood, 1 skip by design; L4 60 files), 0 failures, no flake re-runs needed. Each clause was then scored at the layer its pin reaches (RUNNER rule 6); every clause whose oracle sits below the pin's layer was driven live on a booted showcase or recorded blocked with its fixture.

## Fails: reproduction rule and disposition

Three of the five fails trace to two commits that landed **after** round 1's subject 5fb79bc0: 28a15270 (#32935, fixes #32711, 2026-11-13 00:56Z) and the ADR-0150 child-B refusal 351c22c9 (#32213, fixes #31697) with 51922976 (#32361). In each case the item's own pin was re-pinned to the new shape and is green; only the clause text lags.

1. **records-forms.field-unique-enforcement · A0 · stale spec.**
   Repro: fresh showcase. Author an object `qauniq_item` with `sku` `unique: true`, which is a tenant-scoped composite index. Then `POST /api/v1/data/qauniq_item {name:'r1',sku:'A-1'}` → 201, and `POST {name:'r2',sku:'A-1'}`.
   Expected per the clause: error `A record with this value already exists`, and a developerMessage `…a unique constraint already holds these values…`.
   Actual: 409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION `{"error":"A record with this SKU already exists","developerMessage":"Duplicate record refused on 'QA Unique Item': a unique constraint on 'SKU' already holds this value. No record was written.","field":"sku","object":"qauniq_item"}`. The row count stays 1. Reproduced twice; the item's own dogfood pin `field-unique-rest-refusal` asserts the actual wording and is 5/0 green.
   Disposition: stale spec (28a15270 / #32935). Re-point acceptance[0]'s verify and its sentence in `automated.ref`. See card-api-R1.
2. **api-backend.error-sentences-and-unique-violation-wire-code · A2 · stale spec.**
   Repro: the scratch app `packages/qa/dogfood/test/fixtures/error-sentences-fixture.ts` (`errsent_contact.email` `unique: true`). `POST /api/v1/actions/errsent_contact/ACTION` with a patch that repeats a taken email.
   Expected per the clause: details exactly `{developerMessage, object}` with no `field`. Actual: `{developerMessage, field:'email', object}`.
   Green twice on fresh boots in the HTTP pin `error-sentences-live.dogfood.test.ts`, which now asserts that key set.
   Disposition: stale spec (28a15270 / #32935 deliberately added `field`). A2 should expect `{developerMessage, field, object}`. See card-api-R1.
3. **api-backend.actions-namespace-address · A0 (N2 skipped as stale) · stale spec.**
   Repro: install the scratch pair. qa_a ships object `qa_a_ticket` with an embedded `escalate`; qa_b ships a standalone `escalate` bound to `qa_a_ticket`. As admin, `POST /api/v1/actions/qa_a_ticket/escalate/RID {}`.
   Expected per the clause: qa_a's action runs. Actual: 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT "The action "escalate" is held by 2 packages in this environment and the caller names no package: package "com.qa.addr-a"; package "com.qa.addr-b". …", with `details.candidates` naming both. Reproduced twice, with and without recordId.
   Disposition: stale spec. 351c22c9 (#32213) and 51922976 (#32361) landed exactly the refusal that N2 says "is not landed and stays with #31697". A0 should expect that 409 for this fixture, or the fixture should give the bare call one holder; N2 retires. See card-api-R1. PR #32965 (#32946, merged 04:22Z, after this subject) re-points "actions bare two-holder → 409" and covers it: the item is at revision 3 on main (A0 expects the 409, N2 retired), so no card is filed for this fail.
4. **ai.mcp-read-file-pdf-word-extraction · A3 · assertion defect.**
   Repro: boot with `OS_MCP_READ_FILE_CPU_BUDGET_MS=1`, upload a text-layer PDF to `showcase_invoice_line.receipt` (the item names `showcase_invoice`, which has no file field), then call MCP `read_file`.
   Actual, 2 of 2 calls: `{content:"none", note:"Reading stopped at the CPU-time budget for one file (1 ms) after page 0, so the text is partial. …"}`, with no `truncated` key and no text.
   Control at 40 ms, 2 of 2: `content:"text"`, `truncated:true`, note "…after page 2 of 180…", 8,532 characters of text.
   The product is right: at 1 ms nothing has been read, and `pdfAnswer` (packages/mcp/src/file-content.ts:574) answers 'none' plus the note by design.
   Disposition: assertion defect. The step's budget must let at least one page through (≈40 ms on this machine), and the fixture object should be `showcase_invoice_line`. See card-api-R1.
5. **api-backend.automation-namespace-address · A8 · product defect (low).**
   Repro: stock showcase, as admin, `DELETE /api/v1/automation/showcase/showcase_batch_reminders/runs`. POST and PUT show the same thing.
   Expected: the automation domain's 405, the same answer as the bare `DELETE /api/v1/automation/showcase_batch_reminders/runs`: `Allow: GET` and the dispatcher envelope with `httpStatus:405`.
   Actual: the Hono transport's 405, `Allow: GET, HEAD` and the envelope `{"error":{"code":"METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED","message":"DELETE is not supported for … Allowed: GET, HEAD.","details":{method,path,allowed}}}`.
   The same split shows on GET `/automation/showcase/X/trigger` and GET `/automation/trigger/showcase/X`. Reproduced twice.
   Disposition: product defect. Card: [card-api-1.md](card-api-1.md).

No security finding. No release blocker: the four P0 items in this slice (`access-security.no-active-org-session-semantics`, `ai.mcp-stdio-fail-closed`, `api-backend.packaged-action-disabled-dispatch`, `automation.packaged-flow-disable-durable`) have no failed clause.

## Off-clause probes (rule 8)

About 90 runner-minutes in total, spread across all 70 items' doors as admin, member, anonymous and keyed personas. Boundary classes tried: empty string, missing id, unknown id, wrong type, duplicate entries, terminal-state retries, and below-floor or unparsable ranges. The probes produced cards 2–6 above.

Observed and not filed (no contract states the expected answer; for the seat to rule):
- A tree field accepts a self-parent and a two-cycle through PATCH (200); cascade delete still terminates.
- Unique values are case-sensitive on SQLite.
- The /keys door and the service-account create-key door answer the same expiry-ceiling rule with different codes (API_KEY_EXPIRY_TOO_LONG vs VALIDATION_FAILED).
- An import into a read-only external object answers 200 with ok 0 and errors 1.
- An approver `{type:'user', value:''}` registers, and only the request-level admin_rescue warns.
- `PUT /meta/package/x` says 'package' is not a type, while /meta/types lists it.
- The 409 for toggling a deployment-authored flow still names sys_metadata_activation and the ADR to the caller.
- The metadata plane and the dispatch door disagree on who holds an object-embedded action (bare GET /meta/action/escalate serves qa_b's copy, while dispatch counts both holders).
